     2	
     3	## Source
     4	
     5	URL: https://radar.cloudflare.com/year-in-review/2024
     6	
     7	The Cloudflare Radar 2024 Year in Review provides a comprehensive view of Internet patterns and trends observed through Cloudflare's global network during 2024. The report covers traffic growth, popular services, technology adoption, connectivity disruptions, security threats, and email security trends. Data is derived from Cloudflare's position as a provider protecting and accelerating websites and applications for millions of customers worldwide.
     8	
     9	## Internet Traffic Growth and Popular Services
    10	
    11	Global Internet traffic grew by 17% in 2024, continuing the upward trend driven by increasing reliance on the Internet for communication, commerce, entertainment, and transportation. The trend line starts mid-January to normalize for post-holiday activity.
    12	
    13	Google maintained its position as the most popular Internet service overall, topping the rankings for the second consecutive year. Generative AI continued its rapid rise throughout 2024, while the Metaverse receded into the background. The ranking methodology is based on aggregate data from Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1 DNS resolver.
    14	
    15	| Rank | Service   |
    16	|------|-----------|
    17	| #1   | Google    |
    18	| #2   | Facebook  |
    19	| #3   | Apple     |
    20	| #4   | TikTok    |
    21	| #5   | AWS       |
    22	| #6   | Microsoft |
    23	| #7   | Instagram |
    24	| #8   | YouTube   |
    25	| #9   | Amazon    |
    26	| #10  | WhatsApp  |
    27	
    28	![Top 10 most popular Internet services worldwide](./assets/top-10-internet-services.jpg)
    29	
    30	SpaceX Starlink traffic saw dramatic 3.3x growth during 2024, continuing to bring satellite Internet connectivity to previously underserved locations. Starlink is not yet available globally; the trend line is scaled relative to peak observed request volume.
    31	
    32	![Normalized Starlink traffic worldwide showing 3.3x growth in 2024](./assets/starlink-traffic-growth-2024.jpg)
    33	
    34	## Technology Adoption and Usage Patterns
    35	
    36	Several key adoption metrics emerged from the 2024 data:
    37	
    38	- **Mobile OS**: 33% of traffic came from iOS devices. Apple iOS and Google Android remain the dominant mobile operating systems, with peak Android traffic share exceeding 95% in some regions and peak iOS reaching around 66%.
    39	- **HTTP/3**: 21% of traffic uses HTTP/3, the most recent version of the protocol that runs on top of QUIC, providing faster connections, packet-loss mitigation, and encryption by default.
    40	- **Search Engines**: Google dominates with 89% of search engine referral traffic, followed by Yandex (3.1%), Baidu (2.7%), Bing (2.6%), DuckDuckGo (0.95%), and other engines (2.2%).
    41	- **Browsers**: Chrome remains the most popular browser globally.
    42	- **API Client Languages**: Go is the most popular API client language with approximately 12% of automated API requests, followed by Node.js, Python (9.6%), Java (7.4%), and .NET (3.6%).
    43	
    44	Post-quantum encryption saw a dramatic surge in adoption during 2024. Starting at around 2% of TLS 1.3 traffic in early 2024, adoption jumped sharply following Google Chrome 124 enabling post-quantum key agreement by default on April 17, rapidly climbing to approximately 12-13%. Mozilla Firefox has also started rolling out post-quantum by default, and Apple Safari began initial testing.
    45	
    46	![Post-quantum encrypted traffic worldwide showing rapid adoption after Chrome 124 release](./assets/post-quantum-encryption-adoption.jpg)
    47	
    48	## Internet Connectivity and Disruptions
    49	
    50	Cloudflare observed 225 major Internet disruptions globally in 2024. These outages result from a variety of causes, and the Cloudflare Radar Outage Center tracks their scope and duration using Cloudflare traffic data.
    51	
    52	The leading causes of Internet disruptions were:
    53	
    54	| Cause                | Count |
    55	|----------------------|-------|
    56	| Government Directed  | 116+  |
    57	| Cable Cut            | 41    |
    58	| Unknown              | 16    |
    59	| Power Outage         | 16    |
    60	| Technical Problem    | 9     |
    61	| Military Action      | 9     |
    62	| Weather              | 8     |
    63	| Maintenance          | 4     |
    64	| Cyber Attack         | 4     |
    65	| Natural Disaster     | 1     |
    66	| Fire                 | 1     |
    67	
    68	![Causes of major Internet disruptions observed in 2024](./assets/internet-disruption-causes.jpg)
    69	
    70	IPv6 adoption reached 28% of dual-stack traffic during 2024. Spain recorded the highest download speed among all countries measured.
    71	
    72	41% of global traffic came from mobile devices, reflecting the continued importance of mobile connectivity worldwide.
    73	
    74	## Security Landscape
    75	
    76	Cloudflare mitigated 6.5% of all traffic it processed, indicating the scale of ongoing threats. The Gambling and Games sector was the most attacked industry category. Notably, 68% of global bot traffic originated from just the top 10 countries.
    77	
    78	The Log4j vulnerability (CVE-2021-44228), first disclosed in December 2021, continues to be actively targeted by attackers more than two years later, underscoring the persistent nature of widely known vulnerabilities.
    79	
    80	RPKI (Resource Public Key Infrastructure) valid routes increased by 6.4%, an important step toward improved Internet routing security.
    81	
    82	## Email Security Threats
    83	
    84	Cloudflare's email security analysis revealed that 4.3% of emails processed were malicious. Among those malicious emails, 43% contained a deceptive link designed to trick recipients. The top-level domain .bar originated the largest share of malicious and spam email observed during the year.
    85	
    86	## Key Findings
    87	
    88	- Global Internet traffic grew 17% year-over-year, with Starlink traffic surging 3.3x as satellite connectivity expanded to underserved regions.
    89	- Post-quantum encryption adoption leapt from approximately 2% to 13% of TLS 1.3 traffic following Chrome 124's default enablement in April 2024.
    90	- Government-directed shutdowns remained the leading cause of the 225 major Internet disruptions observed, followed by cable cuts (41 incidents) and power outages (16).
    91	- Security threats remained pervasive: 6.5% of all traffic was mitigated, Gambling/Games was the most targeted sector, and Log4j exploitation persists years after disclosure.
    92	- Go surpassed other languages to become the most popular API client language, capturing roughly 12% of automated API traffic.

    10	# PPT Master Skill
    11	
    12	> AI-driven multi-format SVG content generation system. Converts source documents into high-quality SVG pages through multi-role collaboration and exports to PPTX.

    14	**Core Pipeline**: `Source Document → Create Project → Template Option → Strategist → [Image_Generator] → Executor → Post-processing → Export`

    16	> [!CAUTION]
    17	> ## 🚨 Global Execution Discipline (MANDATORY)
    18	>
    19	> **This workflow is a strict serial pipeline. The following rules have the highest priority — violating any one of them constitutes execution failure:**
    20	>
    21	> 1. **SERIAL EXECUTION** — Steps MUST be executed in order; the output of each step is the input for the next. Non-BLOCKING adjacent steps may proceed continuously once prerequisites are met, without waiting for the user to say "continue"
    22	> 2. **BLOCKING = CONFIRMATION POINT** — Steps marked ⛔ BLOCKING are confirmation checkpoints. If a user is present, pause and wait for confirmation.     23	> 3. **NO CROSS-PHASE BUNDLING** — Cross-phase bundling is FORBIDDEN. Once confirmed (or auto-decided in non-interactive mode), all subsequent non-BLOCKING steps — design spec output, SVG generation, speaker notes, and post-processing — may proceed automatically without further confirmation)
    24	> 4. **GATE BEFORE ENTRY** — Each Step has prerequisites (🚧 GATE) listed at the top; these MUST be verified before starting that Step
    25	> 5. **NO SPECULATIVE EXECUTION** — "Pre-preparing" content for subsequent Steps is FORBIDDEN (e.g., writing SVG code during the Strategist phase)
    26	> 6. **NO SUB-AGENT SVG GENERATION** — Executor Step 6 SVG generation is context-dependent and MUST be completed by the current main agent end-to-end. Delegating page SVG generation to sub-agents is FORBIDDEN

     7	## 1. SVG Banned Features Blacklist
     8	
     9	The following features are **absolutely forbidden** when generating SVGs — PPT export will break if any are used:
    10	
    11	| Banned Feature | Description |
    12	|----------------|-------------|
    13	| `clipPath` | Clipping paths |
    14	| `mask` | Masks |
    15	| `<style>` | Embedded stylesheets |
    16	| `class` | CSS selector attributes (`id` inside `<defs>` is a legitimate reference and is NOT banned) |
    17	| External CSS | External stylesheet links |
    18	| `<foreignObject>` | Embedded external content |
    19	| `<symbol>` + `<use>` | Symbol reference reuse |
    20	| `textPath` | Text along a path |
    21	| `@font-face` | Custom font declarations |
    22	| `<animate*>` / `<set>` | SVG animations |
    23	| `<script>` / event attributes | Scripts and interactivity |
    24	| `marker` / `marker-end` | Line endpoint markers |
    25	| `<iframe>` | Embedded frames |
    26

    29	## 2. PPT Compatibility Alternatives
    30	
    31	| Banned Syntax | Correct Alternative |
    32	|---------------|---------------------|
    33	| `fill="rgba(255,255,255,0.1)"` | `fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.1"` |
    34	| `<g opacity="0.2">...</g>` | Set `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` on each child element individually |
    35	| `<image opacity="0.3"/>` | Overlay a `<rect fill="background-color" opacity="0.7"/>` mask layer after the image |
    36	| `marker-end` arrows | Draw triangle arrows with `<polygon>` |
    37	
    38	**Mnemonic**: PPT does not recognize rgba, group opacity, image opacity, or markers.

    70	## 4. Basic SVG Rules
    71	
    72	- **viewBox** must match the canvas dimensions (`width`/`height` must match `viewBox`)
    73	- **Background**: Use `<rect>` to define the page background color
    74	- **Line breaks**: Use `<tspan>` for manual line breaks; `<foreignObject>` is FORBIDDEN
    75	- **Fonts**: Use system fonts only (Microsoft YaHei, Arial, Calibri, etc.); `@font-face` is FORBIDDEN
    76	- **Styles**: Use inline styles only (`fill="..."` `font-size="..."`); `<style>` / `class` are FORBIDDEN (`id` inside `<defs>` is legitimate)
    77	- **Colors**: Use HEX values; for transparency use `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity`
    78	- **Image references**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`
    79	- **Icon placeholders**: `<use data-icon="icon-name" x="" y="" width="48" height="48" fill="#HEX"/>` (auto-embedded during post-processing)

   108	## 6. Shadow & Overlay Techniques
   109	
   110	> `<mask>` elements and `<image opacity="...">` are banned. Always use stacked `<rect>` or gradient overlays instead (see §2).
   111	
   112	### Shadow
   113	
   114	#### Filter Soft Shadow — Recommended
   115	
   116	Best for: cards, floating panels, elevated elements. `svg_to_shapes.py` automatically converts `feGaussianBlur` + `feOffset` into native PPTX `<a:outerShdw>`.
   117	
   118	```xml
   119	<defs>
   120	  <filter id="softShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
   121	    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="8"/>
   122	    <feOffset dx="0" dy="4" result="offsetBlur"/>
   123	    <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.08" result="shadowColor"/>
   124	    <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
   125	    <feMerge>
   126	      <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
   127	      <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
   128	    </feMerge>
   129	  </filter>
   130	</defs>
   131	<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
   132	```
   133	
   134	Recommended parameters:
   135	```
   136	stdDeviation:   6–10     (smaller = crisper, larger = softer)
   137	flood-opacity:  0.06–0.12  (keep low for a premium feel)
   138	dy:             3–6      (vertical > horizontal for natural top-light)
   139	dx:             0–2
   140	```
   141	
   142	#### Colored Shadow
   143	
   144	Best for: accent buttons, brand-colored cards. Use the element's own color family instead of black.
   145	
   146	```xml
   147	<filter id="colorShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
   148	  <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="10"/>
   149	  <feOffset dx="0" dy="6" result="offsetBlur"/>
   150	  <feFlood flood-color="#1A73E8" flood-opacity="0.20" result="shadowColor"/>
   151	  <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
   152	  <feMerge>
   153	    <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
   154	    <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
   155	  </feMerge>
   156	</filter>
   157	```
   158	
   159	Replace `flood-color` with the element's brand color; keep `flood-opacity` between 0.12–0.20.
   160	
   161	#### Layered Rect Shadow — High-Compatibility Fallback
   162	
   163	Best for: maximum compatibility with older PowerPoint versions. Stack 2–3 semi-transparent rectangles behind the main card:
   164	
   165	```xml
   166	<!-- Shadow layers (back to front, largest offset first) -->
   167	<rect x="68" y="72" width="400" height="240" rx="16" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.03"/>
   168	<rect x="65" y="69" width="400" height="240" rx="14" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.05"/>
   169	<rect x="62" y="66" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#1A73E8" fill-opacity="0.04"/>
   170	<!-- Main card -->
   171	<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
   172	```

   187	  </linearGradient>

- **Key Message**: Global Internet traffic accelerated 17% YoY; satellite connectivity is reshaping access patterns

  - Insight: Metaverse receded into background

### Slide 04 — Post-Quantum Encryption Jumps from 2% to 13% of TLS 1.3
- **Layout**: Left-right split (image left, insights right) or top-bottom
- **Key Message**: Post-quantum encryption saw dramatic adoption; HTTP/3 and Go also gained ground
- **Content Points**:
  - Post-quantum: ~2% → ~12-13% of TLS 1.3 traffic after Chrome 124 (April 17)
  - Firefox rolling out by default; Safari began initial testing
  - HTTP/3: 21% of traffic (QUIC-based, faster, encrypted by default)
  - Go: ~12% of automated API requests (top API client language)
  - Other API languages: Node.js, Python 9.6%, Java 7.4%, .NET 3.6%
  - Mobile: 33% iOS traffic; Android peaks >95% in some regions, iOS ~66%
  - Search: Google 89%, Yandex 3.1%, Baidu 2.7%, Bing 2.6%, DuckDuckGo 0.95%
- **Image**: `post-quantum-encryption-adoption.jpg` (wide landscape)
- **Chart**: `line_chart` for post-quantum trend; `donut_chart` for HTTP/3 share

### Slide 05 — 225 Major Disruptions: Government Shutdowns Lead Outage Causes
- **Layout**: Left-right split (image/table left, insights right) or table dominant
- **Key Message**: 225 major disruptions observed; government-directed shutdowns are the leading cause
- **Content Points**:
  - Total: 225 major Internet disruptions globally in 2024
  - Table of causes: Government Directed 116+, Cable Cut 41, Unknown 16, Power Outage 16, Technical Problem 9, Military Action 9, Weather 8, Maintenance 4, Cyber Attack 4, Natural Disaster 1, Fire 1

  - KPI: 68% of global bot traffic from top 10 countries
  - Most attacked sector: Gambling and Games
  - Log4j (CVE-2021-44228) still actively targeted >2 years after disclosure
  - RPKI valid routes increased 6.4%
  - Email: 4.3% of emails malicious; 43% of malicious emails contained deceptive links
  - TLD .bar originated largest share of malicious/spam email
- **Chart**: `kpi_cards` for 6.5% and 68%

### Slide 07 — Five Takeaways Shaping the 2025 Internet Outlook
- **Layout**: Single column or 5-item vertical list with icons
- **Key Message**: Five strategic findings to inform 2025 planning for network and security leaders
- **Content Points**:
  1. **Traffic Growth Trajectory** — 17% YoY growth + Starlink 3.3x signals expanding global connectivity

     6	
     7	## Role Definition
     8	
     9	An MBB-level (McKinsey / Bain / BCG) top-tier consulting style SVG design executor. Suitable for strategic planning, board presentations, investment roadshows, C-suite decision support, and other **premium consulting** scenarios. Core characteristics: data-driven insights, pyramid-structured narrative, extreme simplicity. Output targets C-level decision-makers.
    10	
    11	---
    12	
    13	## SCQA Framework (Narrative Structure)
    14	
    15	Every MBB-level presentation follows the SCQA narrative structure:
    16	
    17	| Element | Purpose | Typical Pages |
    18	|---------|---------|---------------|
    19	| **S - Situation** | Establish shared context | Cover / Pages 1-2 |
    20	| **C - Complication** | Introduce the problem / tension | Pages 2-3 |
    21	| **Q - Question** | The implicit or explicit question to solve | Transition page |
    22	| **A - Answer** | Core solution | All body pages |
    23	
    24	**Page sequencing**: Cover embodies S+C → Executive Summary answers Q → Chapters develop A → Closing revisits S
    25	
    26	**Title writing**:
    27	
    28	| SCQA Element | Weak Title | MBB-level Title |
    29	|-------------|------------|-----------------|
    30	| S | "Industry Background" | "Digital penetration surpasses 60%, industry enters deep waters" |
    31	| C | "Challenges Faced" | "Yet three structural contradictions constrain scaled deployment" |
    32	| Q | "Strategic Question" | "How to move from pilot to full deployment within 18 months?" |
    33	| A | "Solution" | "Three-phase path: Focus, Expand, Scale" |
    34	
    35	---
    36	
    37	## Data Contextualization (Never Present Data in Isolation)
    38	
    39	> **Golden Rule**: Never display a single data point in isolation. Every number needs context.
    40	
    41	| Method | Pattern | Visual Implementation |
    42	|--------|---------|----------------------|
    43	| **Time comparison** | "From X to Y" | Line chart + arrow annotating magnitude of change |
    44	| **Benchmark** | "X vs industry average Y" | Bar chart with gray dashed baseline |
    45	| **Competitive comparison** | "Us X vs Competitor Y" | Side-by-side bar chart, highlight own data |
    46	| **Target gap** | "Actual X / Target Y" | Progress bar + gap annotation |
    47	| **Ranking** | "Ranked #N of M" | Horizontal bar chart + highlight marker |
    48	
    49	**Data annotation three essentials**: Every data visualization must include (1) The value itself (large bold font) (2) Comparison reference (baseline / prior period / competitor) (3) Meaning interpretation ("So what?")
    50	
    51	```xml
    52	<text x="160" y="280" text-anchor="middle" font-size="42" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">97.3%</text>
    53	<text x="160" y="310" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Industry avg 82% | Competitor A 89%</text>
    54	<text x="160" y="335" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#059669">Leading industry by 15.3 percentage points</text>
    55	```
    56	
    57	---
    58	
    59	## Pyramid Principle (Conclusion First)
    60	
    61	> Executives don't care about your *process* — they care about *results*.
    62	
    63	```
    64	         ┌─────────────────┐
    65	         │  Core Conclusion │   ← Page title / Takeaway
    66	         └────────┬────────┘
    67	      ┌───────────┼───────────┐
    68	  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐
    69	  │ Arg 1 │  │ Arg 2 │  │ Arg 3 │   ← Key supporting points
    70	  └───────┘  └───────┘  └───────┘
    71	```
    72	
    73	| Level | Position | Font Size |
    74	|-------|----------|-----------|
    75	| Core conclusion | Takeaway Box | 16-18px bold |
    76	| Arguments | Content area body | 14-16px |
    77	| Supporting data | Charts / cards | 12-14px |
    78	
    79	**Contrast**: Title "Market Research Results" (wrong) → "Metaverse needs 5-10 years to reach scale" (right); Body "We researched... and found..." (wrong) → "Three arguments: (1)... (2)... (3)..." (right)

   103	### Strategic Roadmap
   104	
   105	Three phases laid out horizontally, `<rect rx="8">` + title + action list, `<polygon>` arrows connecting:

   108	Focus Core (0-6mo)  ──>  Expand Capability (6-12mo)  ──>  Scale Up (12-18mo)

   122	## Strategic Use of Color
   123	
   124	MBB-level color usage is extremely restrained — color serves information:
   125	
   126	| Purpose | Method |
   127	|---------|--------|
   128	| **Focus** | Target data in theme color, everything else gray |
   129	| **Reduce cognitive load** | Same series differentiated by opacity (`fill-opacity` 1.0/0.6/0.3) |
   130	| **Semantics** | Green = positive, Red = negative, Gray = baseline |
   131	| **Branding** | Gradient top bar / decorative lines in brand color |
   132	
   133	**Commandments**: No more than 3 primary colors; accent color used at most 2-3 places globally; data series use same-hue depth variations, not different colors; background white or very light gray.

   137	## Chart vs Table Selection Matrix
   138	
   139	| Scenario | Recommended Form | Reason |
   140	|----------|-----------------|--------|
   141	| Comparing 2-7 categories | **Bar chart** | Visual comparison is intuitive |
   142	| Time trends | **Line chart** | Time series clarity |
   143	| Precise values / large rankings | **Table** | 50 data points in a bar chart would be chaotic |
   144	| Proportional composition | **Donut chart** | More modern than pie charts |
   145	| Two-dimensional positioning | **2x2 matrix** | Strategic quadrant analysis |
   146	| Change attribution | **Waterfall chart** | Factor decomposition |

   150	## Speaker Notes Style
   151	
   152	### Narrative Tone
   153	
   154	Targeting **executives / decision-makers**. Pyramid structure — every sentence carries information. Composed, authoritative, and insightful tone.
   155	
   156	### Stage Direction Markers
   157	
   158	| Marker | Purpose | Example |
   159	|--------|---------|---------|
   160	| `[Pause]` | Silence after key insight, let executives absorb | "This means we are missing a billion-dollar market. [Pause]" |
   161	| `[Scan Room]` | Observe decision-makers' reactions, decide whether to elaborate | "[Scan Room] If there are questions, I can elaborate." |
   162	| `[Data]` | Conversational number delivery | "[Data] 63% → nearly two-thirds" |
   163	| `[Benchmark]` | Emphasize comparison baseline | "[Benchmark] Compared to the industry average of 12%, our 23% is nearly double" |
   164	| `[Transition]` | Bridge from previous page, at start of each page's text | "[Transition] Building on the strategic framework, let's drill into the implementation path." |
   165	
   166	### Notes Writing Guidelines
   167	
   168	- **Pyramid structure**: Conclusion → Arguments → Details
   169	- **Data contextualization**: Every number has a comparison reference
   170	- **Executive language**: "The strategic implication is...", "The core insight is..."
   171	- **Flex mechanism**: Annotate "content that can be skipped if time is tight" for flexible duration
   172	- **Key points structure**: `Key points: (1) Core insight (2) Data support (3) Strategic implication`

   177	# 03_strategic_path
   178	
   179	[Transition] Having clarified the problem and the opportunity, now comes the most critical part — our response path.
   180	
   181	We recommend a three-phase strategy. [Pause]
   182	
   183	Phase one: Focus. Over the next six months, concentrate resources on conquering the Eastern China market.
   184	[Data] Eastern China contributes nearly two-thirds of industry growth, [Benchmark] yet our penetration rate is only half of Competitor A's. [Pause]
   185	
   186	Phase two: Expand. Use Eastern China as a template, replicate to Southern and Northern China.
   187	Phase three: Scale. Leverage a digital platform for nationwide coverage.
   188	
   189	[Scan Room] The resource allocation for phase one is in the appendix — would you like me to walk through it now?
   190	
   191	Key points: (1) Focus-Expand-Scale three-phase approach (2) Data-backed Eastern China priority (3) 18-month full deployment
   192	Duration: 3 minutes
   193	Flex: [If time is tight, skip phase two and three details and go straight to financial impact]
   194	```

# 01_cover

Welcome to the Cloudflare Radar 2024 Year in Review. This executive briefing synthesizes the most significant Internet patterns and trends observed through Cloudflare's global network during 2024 — covering traffic growth, technology adoption, connectivity disruptions, and the evolving security landscape. Our goal is to equip technology executives and network infrastructure leaders with data-driven insights to inform strategic planning for 2025.

Key points: (1) Comprehensive view of 2024 Internet trends (2) Derived from Cloudflare's position protecting millions of customers worldwide (3) Targeted at technology executives and network leaders
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 02_traffic_growth

[Transition] Let's begin with the macro picture: how much did the Internet grow in 2024?

Global Internet traffic grew by 17% year-over-year, continuing the upward trajectory driven by our increasing reliance on the Internet for communication, commerce, entertainment, and transportation. [Data] That's nearly one-fifth growth in a single year. [Pause]

But the more dramatic story is Starlink. SpaceX Starlink traffic surged 3.3x during 2024, bringing satellite Internet connectivity to previously underserved locations. [Benchmark] This is not incremental growth — this is a step-change in how connectivity reaches remote and underserved regions. [Pause]

Supporting this, 41% of global traffic now comes from mobile devices, and iOS captures 33% of mobile traffic. Android still dominates in many regions, peaking above 95% in some markets, while iOS peaks around 66% in its strongest regions. Spain recorded the highest download speed among all countries measured.

Key points: (1) 17% YoY global traffic growth (2) Starlink 3.3x surge signals satellite connectivity expansion (3) Mobile-first reality: 41% of traffic from mobile devices
Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 03_top_services

[Transition] With that growth context, let's look at which services captured the most attention in 2024.

Google maintained its position as the most popular Internet service overall, topping the rankings for the second consecutive year. [Data] The top three — Google, Facebook, Apple — remain unchanged, but the story beneath the surface is more interesting. [Pause]

Generative AI continued its rapid rise throughout 2024, cementing itself as a dominant force in Internet services. Meanwhile, the Metaverse receded into the background as practical AI applications captured both user and enterprise attention. [Benchmark] This is a clear signal of where technology investment and user engagement are flowing. [Pause]

The ranking methodology is based on aggregate data from Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1 DNS resolver, giving us a ground-truth view of actual Internet usage patterns across the globe.

Key points: (1) Google #1 for second consecutive year (2) Generative AI rises as Metaverse fades (3) Ranking based on 1.1.1.1 DNS resolver data
Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 04_tech_adoption

[Transition] Beyond traffic volume and service popularity, let's examine the technology adoption shifts that will shape infrastructure decisions in 2025.

The most striking technology story of 2024 is post-quantum encryption. Starting at approximately 2% of TLS 1.3 traffic in early 2024, adoption jumped sharply following Google Chrome 124 enabling post-quantum key agreement by default on April 17. [Data] Within months, adoption climbed to approximately 12-13%. [Benchmark] That's a 6x increase in under a year. [Pause]

Mozilla Firefox has also started rolling out post-quantum by default, and Apple Safari began initial testing. This means crypto-agility is no longer a niche concern — it's a board-level infrastructure priority.

On the protocol front, HTTP/3 now accounts for 21% of traffic, running on QUIC for faster connections, packet-loss mitigation, and encryption by default. In the developer ecosystem, Go became the most popular API client language with approximately 12% of automated API requests, followed by Python at 9.6%, Java at 7.4%, and .NET at 3.6%.

Key points: (1) Post-quantum encryption 2% → 13% after Chrome 124 (2) HTTP/3 at 21% adoption on QUIC (3) Go leads API client languages at ~12%
Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 05_disruptions

[Transition] Growth and adoption are positive signals, but the Internet's resilience faced serious tests in 2024.

Cloudflare observed 225 major Internet disruptions globally in 2024. The leading cause, by a wide margin, was government-directed shutdowns — accounting for 116 or more incidents. [Data] That's over half of all major disruptions. [Benchmark] Cable cuts, the second-largest cause, accounted for only 41 incidents — less than half the government-directed total. [Pause]

Power outages and unknown causes each contributed 16 incidents, while technical problems and military action each accounted for 9. Weather caused 8 disruptions, and maintenance and cyber attacks each caused 4.

On the connectivity front, IPv6 adoption reached 28% of dual-stack traffic, and 41% of global traffic came from mobile devices. Spain recorded the highest download speed among all countries measured.

Key points: (1) 225 major disruptions globally (2) Government-directed shutdowns = 116+ incidents, the leading cause (3) Cable cuts (41) and power outages (16) follow
Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 06_security

[Transition] Finally, let's examine the security landscape — because threats did not stand still in 2024.

Cloudflare mitigated 6.5% of all traffic it processed. [Data] That means nearly one in fifteen requests was malicious enough to require active mitigation. [Pause] The Gambling and Games sector was the most attacked industry category. Notably, 68% of global bot traffic originated from just the top 10 countries — a striking concentration.

The Log4j vulnerability, first disclosed in December 2021, continues to be actively targeted by attackers more than two years later. [Benchmark] This is a critical reminder that known vulnerabilities don't age out of the threat landscape — they persist as long as unpatched systems remain exposed. [Pause]

On the email security front, 4.3% of emails processed were malicious. Among those, 43% contained a deceptive link designed to trick recipients. The .bar top-level domain originated the largest share of malicious and spam email observed during the year.

On a positive note, RPKI valid routes increased by 6.4%, an important step toward improved Internet routing security.

Key points: (1) 6.5% of traffic mitigated (2) Log4j still actively targeted >2 years post-disclosure (3) 4.3% malicious emails, 43% with deceptive links
Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 07_takeaways

[Transition] To close, here are the five strategic takeaways that should shape your 2025 planning.

First, traffic growth trajectory. 17% YoY growth plus Starlink's 3.3x surge signals expanding global connectivity. Plan infrastructure for sustained demand.

Second, post-quantum momentum. The 2% to 13% leap in TLS 1.3 means crypto-agility is now a board-level priority. Audit your encryption roadmaps now. [Pause]

Third, connectivity fragility. Government-directed shutdowns at 116+ incidents remain the number one disruption cause. Diversify paths and build resilience into your network architecture.

Fourth, persistent security threats. 6.5% mitigation rate, Log4j still exploited, and email threats at 4.3% mean defense-in-depth and patching discipline are non-negotiable. [Pause]

Fifth, the evolving developer ecosystem. Go leads API clients at approximately 12%, and HTTP/3 at 21% is reshaping protocols. Align your architecture with these modern stack trends.

[Scan Room] These five trends represent both opportunity and risk. The organizations that plan for them in 2025 will be best positioned to capitalize on the next wave of Internet growth.

Key points: (1) Five strategic takeaways for 2025 planning (2) Traffic, crypto, resilience, security, and developer ecosystem (3) Actionable recommendations for each
Duration: 3 minutes
